instruction: Open the 2022 book reading spreadsheet on the desktop. Find the book written by the author whose name comes first alphabetically. Write the book title to 'book_list_result.docx' on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the book by the author whose name comes first alphabetically. Verified with Python: All authors appear once in the list. Authors sorted alphabetically: Aldous Huxley, Arthur C. Clarke, C.S. Lewis, Dan Brown, George R. R. Martin, Michael Crichton, Neil Gaiman, Shusaku Endo, Stephen King, Toni Morrison. Aldous Huxley comes first, and wrote 'Brave New World'. The evaluator checks if the DOCX file contains 'Brave New World'.

llm_judge_reasons: Metric function correctly handles expected parameter: Line 16 properly extracts text from dict with 'expected.get('text') if isinstance(expected, dict) else expected'.
When expected.type='rule', the framework calls get_rule() which returns config['rules'] ({'text': 'Brave New World'}), and the metric correctly extracts the text value.
Getter logic is correct: extracts all text content from DOCX file and returns it as a string, which is the right state for this task.
Metric comparison logic is correct: performs case-insensitive substring matching after normalizing whitespace, appropriate for checking if the book title appears in the document.
Expected value 'Brave New World' is semantically correct: metadata explains that Aldous Huxley comes first alphabetically among all authors and wrote this book.
Postconfig is appropriate: activates the Writer window and saves the document with Ctrl+S to ensure the file state is persisted before evaluation.
Complete coverage: the evaluator checks the only requirement - that the correct book title was written to the DOCX file.
Edge case handling: metric returns 0.0 if result or expected_text are not strings, preventing crashes on missing/empty data.
